elements.text: Blue Nude II was completed in 1952.
elements.source_sentence: The second in the series, Blue Nude II, was completed in 1952.

elements.text: The painted gouache cut-outs that compose the Blue Nudes were inspired by Matisse's collection of African sculpture and his visit to Tahiti.

elements.text: After his death, the works were printed in a special 1956 issue of Verve, entitled 'Les Dernières Œuvres de Matisse'.

elements.text: The series was later shown at the Museum of Modern Art (MoMA) from October 2014 to February 2015 as part of the exhibition Henri Matisse: The Cut-Outs.

elements.text: Blue Nude II is part of the collection at the Musée national d’art moderne/Centre de création industrielle, Centre Georges Pompidou, Paris.

elements.text: Matisse’s cut-outs, including Blue Nude II, often appear effortless, but the work was arduous and sometimes he struggled.

elements.text: Matisse aimed to unite color and drawing in his work, including Blue Nude II.

elements.text: Matisse experienced frustration while creating the Blue Nudes, which led him to stop cutting and turn to drawing.

elements.text: Matisse learned to cut into the paper and shift the two sides apart to describe the form in his cut-outs.
